    Power for the PPI++ mean estimator

    power_ppi_pp_mean.Rd

    Computes two-sided normal-theory power for the PPI++ mean estimator. You can supply raw variance pieces (sigma_y2, sigma_f2, cov_y_f, var_f, var_res) or reuse the metrics interface (metrics, metric_type, m_labeled, correction) to back out the required inputs.

    power_ppi_pp_mean(
  delta,
  N,
  n,
  alpha = 0.05,
  sigma_y2 = NULL,
  sigma_f2 = NULL,
  cov_y_f = NULL,
  var_f = NULL,
  var_res = NULL,
  metrics = NULL,
  metric_type = NULL,
  m_labeled = n,
  correction = TRUE,
  lambda = NULL,
  lambda_type = c("oracle", "user")
)

    Arguments

    delta

    Effect size \(\theta - \theta_0\).

    N

    Unlabeled sample size.

    n

    Labeled sample size.

    alpha

    Two-sided significance level (default 0.05).

    sigma_y2

    Variance of the outcome Y; overrides the value inferred from metrics.

    sigma_f2

    Variance of the predictions f(X); overrides the value inferred from metrics.

    cov_y_f

    Optional population moments. These override values inferred from metrics or var_f/var_res.

    var_f, var_res

    Optional variance pieces for the vanilla PP estimator.

    metrics

    Optional list of predictive-performance summaries.

    metric_type

    Character string describing the metric bundle (e.g., "continuous", "hard", "prob").

    m_labeled

    Labeled sample size associated with the metrics (defaults to n).

    correction

    Logical; apply finite-sample variance corrections (default TRUE).

    lambda

    Optional user-specified blend weight.

    lambda_type

    "oracle" (default) uses the closed-form blend; "user" evaluates power at the supplied lambda.

    Value

    Scalar power in [0, 1].
